newsitem.title: USA: Aetna's Sebastianelli resigns as president.
newsitem.headline: Aetna's Sebastianelli resigns as president.

text.p: Aetna Inc said Friday that president Joseph Sebastianelli had resigned, effective June 1.

Sebastianelli, 50, considered by analysts to be one of the top candidates to succeed Ronald Compton as chairman and chief executive of the insurance company, attributed the move to a conflict with his personal life.
"I have found that the demands of my job and my personal responsibilities, including my family, are incompatible," he said in a statement issued by the company Friday evening.

"Obviously, I did not anticipate that this conflict would arise when I accepted this position. Ron Compton and the Aetna board of directors have been fully supportive of me, and I leave with deep regrets and with total confidence in the future of Aetna," he said.
Sebastianelli was named president of the $15 billion-a-year insurer less than three months ago.
Aetna said Compton, who is scheduled to retire as chairman and chief executive on March 1, 1998, would assume the title of president.
"He is assuming the presidency as of now. Whether he holds that to his retirement or not, I could not say," said company spokeswoman Joyce Oberdorf.
Oberdorf declined to provide financial details of Sebastianelli's resignation.
Earlier this week Aetna said it would pay Sebastianelli more than $2 million if he was not named chief executive within a year.

The company said it would pay Sebastianelli severance equal to three times his base salary and target annual bonus if he was not offered the top spot by February 28, 1998, and if he quit within a year of that date.
Sebastianelli was co-president of Pennsylvania-based U.S. Healthcare before Aetna bought the company last July. His annual base salary at Aetna was to be $725,000 this year.
Besides Sebastianelli, analysts also considered Aetna's vice chairman for strategy and finance, Richard Huber, as a possible successor to Compton.
